the Landau-de-Gennes theory of liquid crystalline self-assembly is a useful tool in understanding the formation of helicoidal plywood structures in biological materials and in the development of biomimetic materials for applications in nanotechnology, biotechnology and tissue engineering.
the Landau-deGennes model can be used to model the textures observed in the cell walls of plants.

the observed defect textures in plant-based helical structures can be modeled by a chiral nematic phase and that the viscoelastic parameters that lead to the observed textures are consistent with those reported in the literature.

understanding the fundamental principles of the self-assembly processes of liquid crystalline polymorphism and their relation to the formation of the plywood architecture in plant cells.
the study of the self-assembly of chiral nematic (cholesteric) liquid crystals in the presence of a secondary phase representing a cell wall in plant-based materials.
the modeling of liquid crystalline self-assembly in the context of plant cell wall architecture and the development of biomimetic ply woods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-assembly model, with the parameters estimated from the analysis of the textures, provides a good description of the plywood architecture.
the liquid crystalline self-assembly postulates are indeed valid and that the liquid crystallinity in the cell wall is a consequence of the self-assembly process.
plant-based liquid crystal analogues are truly liquid crystalline in nature and the self-assembly postulated mechanism is the most likely mechanism for formation of the plywood architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are using a liquid crystal theory to explain the formation of textures in the solid state of plant cell walls, where the textures are formed by the self-assembly of liquid crystals.
the liquid crystal self assembly model is able to predict the observed textures in plant cell walls.
we are able to show that the self assembly model of plant based liquid crystalline polymorphs is a viable model and is able to predict the textures observed in nature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed textures and defects are a direct result of self assembly of a liquid crystalline phase, and not the result of a random assembly process.

the observed textures in the domain of plant-based helicoidal plywood are consistent with a liquid crystalline phase and the model provides a quantitative description of the visco-elastic material parameters required to obtain these textures.
plant-based liquid crystalline materials can be used as templates to design new functional materials with unique properties and functions.
